title: KPI experiment scratchpad — personal OKR draft
content:
Status: messy scratchpad for personal KPI experiments and a first-pass OKR draft

Context / goal
- Need a tight set of personal KRs aligned to org goal: reduce cost per 1M tokens while keeping p95 latency \u003c= 400ms for common routes.
- This doc is my running notes: experiments run, quick retros, next actions, and a 6-week OKR draft to present at 1:1.

Quick metrics (baseline snapshot)
- Route: /v1/generate (priority production traffic)
- Baseline (Feb 14): p50=120ms, p95=520ms, tokens/sec=180, cost per 1k tokens = $0.42 (estimated infra)
- Traffic mix: 65% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% med (128-512), 10% long (>512)
- Baseline quality: acceptance rate on eval sets = 92%

Hypothesis matrix (what I'm testing)
1) Batch-size tuning: dynamic batch max 8 vs 16 vs 32
   - Hypothesis: small batches improve tail latency for short prompts; medium batches improve throughput for long ones.
2) Prefix cache aggressive eviction policy (LRU -> TTL 5m) + sticky routing to cached hosts
   - Hypothesis: prefix cache will reduce p50 for conversational flows by ~15% and reduce token cost by reducing recompute.
3) Quantization experiment: q3_k -> q4_0 fallback profile on lower-tier nodes for non-PII traffic
   - Hypothesis: cut token compute cost by ~18% while keeping eval acceptance > 90%.
4) Early-exit decoding (top-k relaxed at token 256 for repetitive prompts)
   - Hypothesis: avoid token churn on long completions; saves tokens for <10% of requests.

Experiment log (runbook style)
- 2026-02-22: Batch 8 -> 16 on staging (A/B) for 48h, sample 30k requests.
  Observations: p50 improved 8ms on 8->16 for med prompts, p95 worsened by 30ms on short prompts. Cost flat.
  Notes: need to route short prompts to small-batch workers. Ticketed: JIRA RI-4782 (owner: me)

- 2026-02-28: Prefix cache TTL=5m rollout to canary (10%), sticky routing to cached hosts.
  Observations: conversational eval set p50 down 18%, p95 down 12% for that flow. Cold start rate increased for new sessions.
  Action: add sticky session header in SDK, update SDK PR (see GH 2485).

- 2026-03-05: q4_0 profile on dedicated low-tier pool (non-sensitive traffic) for 72h.
  Observations: cost-per-token decreased ~16% on pool. Some hallucination rate up slightly on long-form tests (from 7%->9%).
  Action: add a fallback check: if rerank-score drops >0.05, route to higher-precision model.

Retrospective notes (what worked / surprises)
- Working: prefix cache produced the biggest consistent win for chat flows with short-turn repeats. Sticky routing is low-effort / high ROI.
- Surprise: batching gains are orthogonal to cache; mixing them without routing rules increases p95.
- Risk: q4_0 introduces brittle edge cases on policy-sensitive prompts; need regression guardrail set on eval prompts.

Personal OKR draft (6-week sprint window)
- Objective: Make inference for product-chat routes materially cheaper and faster without degrading output quality.
  KR1: Reduce p95 latency for /v1/generate on chat flows from 520ms -> 380ms (production simulated window)
  KR2: Reduce infra cost per 1M tokens for these routes by 15% (measured across Dedicated + Hosted mix)
  KR3: Create and run 3 automatic regression evals (prompt sets) with alerting and a weekly quality dashboard
  Confidence: 6/10 (prefix cache + routing seems achievable; quantization risk reduces confidence)
  Owner: Sophie Nguyen (me)

Weekly check-in (this week)
- Done:
  - Completed q4_0 canary and dashboarding of basic metrics (cost, p95, acceptance)
  - Filed routing rules experiment (JIRA RI-4831) to split short vs med/long prompt traffic
- Blockers:
  - Need SDK change merged to surface sticky-session header (PR waiting on security review)
  - Need a small eval compute budget approved for nightly regression runs (asking Arjun)
- Next actions for next 7 days:
  1) Deploy routing rule to 20% (short prompts -> small-batch pool) and measure p95 delta by prompt-length bucket (owner: me)
  2) Add fallback reroute on low-quality detection for q4_0 traffic (owner: me + infra)
  3) Draft OKR slide for 1:1 (two bullets, metrics snapshot, ask: 1 FTE time for automation)

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Could try adaptive batch ceilings: small initial batch for first 10ms, then expand if queue grows. Might reduce cold-tail latency.
- Investigate kernel selection logs to see if small vs large batch differences are due to different gemm kernels being chosen.
- Consider running quality evals stratified by prompt archetype (instruction, chat, summarization) not just token length.

Questions for 1:1 with Arjun (tomorrow)
- Do we have runway to allocate one SRE/infra sprint for routing rule automation? (need ~1 week of dev + canary work)
- Approve $X for nightly compute budget to run 3 regression evals. Suggest starting with 10k prompts/night (cost estimate attached in Confluence link).
- Triage decision: acceptable KR tradeoff threshold for q4_0: if eval acceptance drops >1.5% do we rollback immediately? propose auto-rollback trigger.

Misc links and references
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2485 (SDK sticky session header)
- JIRA: RI-4782 (batching experiments), RI-4831 (routing rules)
- Confluence notebook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Throughput-benchmark-notes

Quick TODO (one-liners)
- [ ] deploy routing 20% by Thu
- [ ] add fallback route for q4_0 by Fri
- [ ] write OKR slide + ask for 1:1 approval
- [ ] ping security for SDK header review

End of scratchpad. Keep pruning, test on staging more, stop overfitting to weird long prompts.
